terms.comment: Literally “flame is always next to smoke”. In Plautus a warning that the slightest approach to wrong leads to it.

evidence: Plaut. Curc. 1.1.53, given so as a proverb by Lewis & Short s.v. flamma
terms.comment: Plautus’s line without semper, as Lewis & Short quotes the proverb.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
